annotations.text:
Matrix Watchface - Amazfit T-Rex 3 Pro 48mm (480 x 480 round, deviceSource 10551552 / 10551553 / 10551555, API 4.2)
Option F as the base: phosphor CRT with scanlines, bloom and a travelling band. Rain at density 48 and speed 1.5, time exactly centred, > SYS.TIME and the blinking cursor stay.

The face runs live: seconds flap every second, steps every 4 s, heart rate every 5 s. On a jump from 9 to 2 the reel rolls forward through 0 and 1 - like a split-flap display. The fine dark line across every digit is the flap edge.
HH:MM sits exactly in the centre of the screen; seconds and cursor hang to the right of it, so the time never shifts while flapping.

Always-on: the readout only, no Matrix rain, no seconds, no flapping - the rain really is the most expensive part.
Digits as a 2px outline at exactly the same position and size as in the active state, so nothing jumps when switching. Black background, well under the 10% pixel limit.
First round and further ideas - kept for reference only. F became the active face on page 1.
The time IS the rain: a 25 x 7 kana grid in which the bright cells form the time.
Dense rain all the way to the edge, solid digits, seconds as an arc along the rim.
Rain only around the edge, a terminal printout in the middle.
Nine slow columns, hollow digits, very few lit pixels.
The rain resolves into the time on wrist raise - shown here with the last digit still running.
The time hangs in the rain as a bright strand, hour above minute.

The terminal classic: narrow, tall, hard corners, not a single round curve. True monospace, every digit the same width - which is what the flap reel needs.
Closest to the CRT look. Downside: very thin, the weakest candidate on the wrist in sunlight.

A hard pixel grid, every digit made of visible blocks. The most angular thing there is, and it fits the kana rain next to it.
Downside: proportional, no equal-width digits - the flap reel would need the cells to stay fixed. At small sizes it quickly looks restless.

Cut corners instead of rounding, technical, very legible - the calmest of the four.
Downside: reads more like a sci-fi interface than Matrix, and it is proportional.

Dot matrix: the digits are made of individual dots, like an LED display. The closest relative to the glyph-time idea from the first round.
Downside: it falls apart at small sizes, which is why only the time is large here.

Typeface proposals - the same face in four cuts. All four are under the Open Font License, so they may be bundled.
The kana rain stays the same in every variant: none of these fonts contains katakana, so the system falls back to its CJK font. Only the time, the labels and the data rows change.
